title: Fitting GPT-2 XL batch 32 onto one 80 GB H100
caption: Each bar is one step's resident training state after applying the technique above the last. Static state never moves -- 24 GB under both FP32 Adam and mixed-precision Adam (16 B/param either way). Only activations shrink: halved by FP16, then the ~201 GB of quadratic score matrices removed by FlashAttention, then halved again by the 16-sequence micro-batch. The H100's capacity is 80 GB -- only the last bar fits. Segment checkpointing reaches ~35.5 GB instead, at +33% arithmetic.

title: Where the peak actually goes
caption: Each bar is the hardware's peak budget; only the left segment is credited model arithmetic. MT-NLG ran at 30.2% MFU and PaLM at 46.2% (PaLM paper, useful-FLOP convention); the chapter's GPT-2 XL model assumes 50%. The uncolored share is everything eta_hw absorbs -- memory stalls, pipeline bubbles, rematerialization, synchronization. Busy-time monitors would report the same runs near 100%.

title: Splitting a fixed batch grows the sync share
caption: GPT-2 XL's ~12 ms AllReduce is ~2% of a step when each replica computes the full batch-32 gradient, but ~14% when the same batch is split eight ways: per-replica arithmetic falls with the local batch while the ~1.75x gradient volume stays fixed. The mechanism behind 'speedup < N' -- arithmetic divides, the synchronization bill does not. Illustrative shares at the chapter's constants, not a measured profile.
